scope: Proposition 6.1 (A gap for bit comparisons) of the manuscript “Constant-factor hardness of Min-UnCut” (preprints/Constant-factor-hardness-of-Min-UnCut-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3300408a7ae8900e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed integer J ≥ 20, effective choices of constants give a four-test comparison system with the following properties. It is constructed from the uniform equation list in Theorem 2.2, for a fixed completeness error ζ > 0 chosen by the construction. Every test compares two bits in folded proof tables, and its contribution to cost is its failure probability divided by a positive rational budget bj. In the YES case there are proof tables of cost at most 4; in the NO case every collection of proof tables has cost greater than J. Alphabet sizes are bounded by effective constants depending only on J, and all local numerical parameters depend only on J.
